newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week April 4 April 11 1997.
**APRIL 4*

BUDAPEST - Privately-owned Moldavian Airlines says it planned this year to carry 14 tonnes of day-old chicks on chartered IIyushin 11-18 'coot' aircraft from Budapest to the Moloovan capital of Chisinau.
NEW DELHI - The Indian government says it gave Gulf Air and Kuwait airways six months to sell their stakes in private Indian carrier Jet Airways.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong Dragon Airlines says it is in negotiations with the Japanese government for approval to start new services to Niigata and Komatsu.
FRANKFURT - Italian regional airline Air Dolomiti says it has expanded seat capacity from Italy to Germany by 25 percent under its summer timetable effective March 30.

MOSCOW - Russian air freight forwarders called on customs authorities to revoke new rules that have caused a backlog of million of dollars worth of imported cargo in Moscow since they were imposed last month.
BUDAPEST - Riga airport says it expects its cargo business to rise as much as 10 percent this year on the strength of growing traffic to Britain and the former Soviet Union.
PARIS - DHL says it hoped to decide on the location of its Rhine Valley hub by the summer.
* DHL Aviation says it hoped to be operating Airbus 300 freighter aircraft on its intra-European services later this year.
FRANKFURT - Dresden airport says it introduced new rules tightening restrictions on night flights from March 30.
STOCKHOLM - SAS says it will drop the cargo fuel surcharge in April if jet fuel prices keep falling.

ZURICH - Sair Group, the newly-created holding company that includes Swissair, says it operating profits in 1996 rose 40 percent, but provisions and the write-down of its stake in Sabena, pushed the group into a new loss of 497 million Swiss francs.
AMSTERDAM - Asiana says it has gained scheduled rights into Schiphol and is set to start a weekly freight operation on May 17.
* Most of Martinair's belly-hold capacity to North America has been bought by Speed Handling Services.
OSTEND - Ostend airport says air cargo traffic in February fell to 7,145 tonnes from 8,094 tonnes in the same month 1996.
BUDAPEST - Riga international airport says its cargo trade fell by 7.9 percent in February 1997, against February 1996.
HERNDON, Va - World Airways says it had named Russell Ray Jr as interim president and chief executive, suceeding Charles Pollard.

ST.LOUIS - TWA says its March 1997 capacity and traffic declined from year-ago levels because of a planned short-term reduction in flying to make more aircraft available for scheduled maintenance and the planned downsizing of aircraft on some international routes.
MEXICO CITY - Mexico's state airport governing body expectsd airport traffic in 1997 to rise by 13 percent to 52 million passengers.
**APRIL 5**

BOMBAY - Analysts and businessmen says a recent flip-flop in Indian aviation policy barring foreign airline policy barring foreign airlines from taking stakes in the domestic sector sends worrisome signals about the pace of ecomonic reform.
**APRIL 6**
BEIJING - The China Daily Business Weekly says airfreight grew faster than all other forms of transport in China in January, outpacing passenger travel.
SHARJAH - Industry executives says the international express market is witnessing significant growth across the globe, outperforming the annual growth of air cargo as a whole.
* Boeing regional director David Pierce says airfreight growth will outpace passenger air traffic growth in all major markets for the next 20 years.
ATLANTA - Delta Air Lines says that it will have 611 daily departures at the Hartsfield Atlanta International airport under its summer 1997 schedule.
**APRIL 7**
HONG KONG - Taiwan carrier China Airlines says it was airming to facilitate its globalisation plan through the sale of a 16 percent existing stake by its majority shareholder to a strategic partner.

JOHANNESBURG -Business Day newspaper says state-run SAA will show an unaudited loss of 345 million rand for the financial year ended March 1997, but has budgeted to break even during the current year.
NEW YORK - The Wall Street Journal says boeing ius getting ready to boost its production rates for all planes by 10 percent beyond the previously-announced levels.

HONG KONG - Taiwan's China Airlines, a major carrier on the Taiwan-Hong Kong route says it may consider alternatives for its China-bound passengers if the charges at Hong Kong's new airport were doubled.
PARIS - Boeing chairman and chief executive Phil Condit says it hopes its planned merger with McDonnell Douglas will obtain the necessary approvals this summer.
HONG KONG - Macau airport says it recorded its second highest cargo tonnage total in March since opening in November 1996.
SHARJAH - Hugh Doyle, managing director of Unisys says the traditional freight industry is failing to meet shippers' demands and integrators are taking the lead in customer satisfaction.
* Doyle says airports have to rethink their role in air cargo to become less of a storage area and more of a conduit for freight.
ROME - Union and comapny sources says unions representing workers at UPS Italia met the company's local management to discuss the latter's plan to layoff 150 out of 900 workers.
LONDON - Expeditors says it has boosted its senior management in Asia as part of an expansion programme there.

PARIS - Air France says that start of a transatlantic alliance with two major U.S. carriers, Delta Air Lines and Continental, part of a strategy to form global links vital to the French state-owned carrier's future.
HONG KONG - The U.S. signed an important air services agreement with Hong Kong guaranteeing its future aviation links after the British-rules territory's return to China later this year.
LONDON - BA says it has awarded Premier Magazines a three-year contract to publish its five in-flight magazines.
TUNIS - An official report showed Tunisia plans to buy nine aircraft between 1997 and 2001, including seven to replace part of the fleet of the national airline Tunis Air.
SHARJAH - An air cargo consultant says electronic data interchange is an essential and strategic tool for the survival of the air cargo industry.
HONG KONG - Cathay says it carried 17.6 percent more cargo traffic during February 1997 compared to February 1996.
* Cathay says it plans to re-start its freighter service to Chicago which it handed over to its 75 percent all-cargo subsidiary AHK Air Kong Kong nine months ago.
SOFIA - Bulgaria's state-run Balkan Airlines plans to stabilise its finances by restructuring its debt before the firm is offered for sale.
ROISSY, France - Air France announced the start of an alliance with U.S. carrier Delta Air Lines and Continental, part of a strategy to form global links to the state-owned airline's future.
zagreb - Croatian flag carrier Croatia Airlines says it expected a net profit in the region of $5 million for 1996, compared to a $3.44 million 1995 loss.
FRANKFURT - TNT Logistik says it has won the first round of a fight to save a parcels contract with Deutsche Post worth several million marks.
MINNEAPOLIS - Northwest Airlines says it launched nonstop service from Minnepolis to Osaka.
WARSAW - DHL says its Polish union expect 1997 sales revenues to rise to $24 million from $16.5 million in 1996.
ROME - Air Dolomitit says it launched a daily ATR 42 return flight -- excluding Saturdays -- between Pisa and Barcelona.
PARIS - ADP says it will send an air cargo task force on missions to Latin America and the U.S. in the autumn.
SANTIAGO - Chile's largest airline Lan Chile says it plans to increase it capital by $70 million.
SEATTLE - Boeing says it delivered 69 commerical and non-commerical aircraft during the first three months of 1997.
PARIS - TNT says it has upgrades its Strasbourg and Bordeaux-Merignac facilities.

VALLETTA - Malta and India says it reached an air services agreement allowing Air Malta and Air India to operate scheduled flights between the two countries without any restrictions on the type of aircraft.
NEW YORK - Air Jamaica says it has expanded its schedule to include five weekly DC-8 freighter flights from Miami to Montego Bay and Kingston, beginning May 1.
SEATTLE - Boeing says it is considering raising production rates beyond the record 40 jets per month already planned for the fourth quarter.
NEW YORK - US Airways Group says it will cut aboutr 240 full-time and part-time customer service and maintenance workers in Baltimore.

WASHINGTON - The General Accounting office says U.S. airports will need between $1.4 billiob and $10.1 billion annually in the next five years to repair runways, build new terminals and meet other infrastructure needs.
MIAMI - Officials at Miami International airport says despite a dip in cargo volumes in February they expected heathly growth would resume.
**APRIL 8**
TOKYO - Japan Airlines says it expects to post a parent operating profit of 28 billion yen in the year to March 31 -- up from its break-even estimate for 1996/97.
SINGAPORE - The U.S. and Singapore signed an open skies agreement lifting restriuctions on air services between the two countries.

BEIJING - China cast doubt on the prospect of finalising in May a contract with an Airbus-led consortium for a joint venture to build a 100-seat jet, saying the European side needed to do much more work on the deal.
MANILA - UPS says it will start flying six times a week to the Philippines.
STOCKHOLM - Lufthansa Cargo says that it has put a second weekly Boeing 747F Jumbo freighter onto the Stockholm-Frankfurt route.
FRANKFURT - U-Freight says it will push ahead with large-scale investments investment in terminals, technology and new services this year.
* U-Freight says it will expand its presence in China this year as the giant market continued to grow strongly.
* U-Freight says clients were tracking and tracing air cargo shipments up to 1,000 times a day through its Internet site.
FRANKFURT - Air Zimbabwe says it is seeking general cargo sales agents for a planned string of new European flights from this October.
JOHANNESBURG - Industry sources say BA and Deutsche Lufthansa have both expressed an interest in acquiring a strategic equity stake in SAA, which the government plans to privatise.
* A formal complaint by SAA against a tie-up between BA and local South Africa carrier Comair has been overuled, the two allied airlines said.
PARIS - ADP figures show full freighter flights at the Paris airports in January and February 1997, totalled 3,475, an increase of 20.5 percent on the same period the previous year.
AMSTERDAM - KLM Cargo says it is planning to introduce a range of new airfreight products aimed at industrial shippers.
* The Dutch shippers organisation says it expects KLM to drop its cargo fuel surcharge on April 15.
FRANKFURT - Air Zimbabwe says it expected its air cargo volumes in Germany to rise to 400 tonnes this year after it took control of its own sales activities.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong's airport authority defended the charges it plans to levy on use of the territory's future Chek Lap Kok airport arging they were "fair, reasonable and competitive".
AMSTERDAM - Aerolineas Argentinas says it will double freighter flights to Buenos Aires from Maastricht Aachen airport this weekend to meet strong demand.
HONG KONG - Cathay says it is projecting a 2.8 percent rise in available FTK's for cargo in 1997 and a 4.5 percent rise in overall route network ATK's.
FRANKFURT - Czech airline CSA says it has increased seat capacity between Germany and the Czech Republic by 50 percent this summer.
* CSA says it aims to increase air cargo sales revenue in Germany by 20 percent to more than one million marks this year.
HONG KONG - AHK Air Hong Kong, which is handing back its trans-Pacific service to parent company Cathay, says it plans to increase capacity on European and Japanese destinations instead.
FRANKFURT - Schenker says it has increased South American logstics services through an agreement with Argentina forwarder Transportes Ader.
MIAMI - According to airport officials computer and telecommunications equipment shipped through Miami international airport will nearly double over the next four years.
LONDON - BA confirmed confirmed that the head of the airline's biggest cabin crew was fired for assaulting another employee, following a row over allegations of being a "fat cat" union boss.
* Privately-owned U.S. all cargo carrier Southern Air Transport says it will introduce into service a fourth Boeing 747-200 freighter in August and up to five more by 2000.
HONG KONG - FedEx says it has extened its U.S.-China and China-Asia to four direct flights weekly.

LONDON - Rickenbacker Port Authority executive director Bruce Millar says the state of Ohio is offering DHL s multi-million dollar incentive package to transfer its U.S. hub to the all cargo Rickenbacker airport.
* Souther Air Transport says it might consider a public share flotation, "but there are no plans to do so".
PARIS - Air France says it had negotiated an agreement with French government authorities making trucked airfreight exempt from a weekend ban on most truck movements.
* Air France says it has signed an agreement with Royal Air Maroc to increase cooperation between the two carriers.
ATLANTA - FedEx says it may consider offering discounts on services purchased through its site on the Internet.
**APRIL 9**
REDWOOD CITY - Emery Worldwide says it has named Kent Scott vice president and chief operating officer of air operations.
PARIS - Marc Rochet, chairman of TAT and Air Liberte says that he sought wage cuts, particularly at TAT, to cut their losses to 300 frances in 1997 from 1.2 billion last year.
PARIS - An upgrading of AOM French Airlines' passenger service to Australia and the South Pacific, will boost freight services on the route, the French airline's cargo director Bernard Tetu says.
ROME - Forli airport authority says air cargo traffic handled at Forli airport in Italy fell three percent in March 1997 to 424 tonnes compared to the same period 1996.
HELSINKI - Finnair Oy says that the group's 1996/1997 operating earning to end-March were clearly weaker than in 1995/96.

BEIJING - Company officials says Saab Aircraft International is urging China it develop local air routes, saying passengers on smaller commuter aircraft alone cvould total 100 million a year within 20 years.

ROME - The Lazio administrative court says it rejected an appeal by Alitalia opposing the granting of a temporary licence to private sector carrier, Air One to carry passengers and cargo between Milan and Rome.
LONDON - Southern Air Transport says it had appointed J Robert Peart as senior vice-president of finance and corporate planning.
GENEVA - IATA says Singapore's Changi and Britain's Manchester have been voted the world's top two airports by long-haul airline passengers.
